top.title: Empire State Building glows gold for NASA's Voyager spacecraft | Space photo of the day for Nov. 19, 2026
top.description: null The Empire State Building is illuminated in gold to celebrate Voyager 1 hitting one light-day from Earth, seen here on Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026, from SUMMIT One Vanderbilt in New York City. (Image credit: NASA/Bill Ingalls) The Empire State Building glowed in glittering gold last night (Nov. 17) to celebrate NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft hitting one light-day from Earth. And it isn't the only building celebrating this achievement with a sparkling display. What is it? Today (Nov. 18) at 5:16 a.m. EST (1016 GMT), NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft hit one light-day from Earth. About 16 billion miles (about 26 billion kilometers) away, this is the point at which it takes a full day (or 24 hours) for one light particle to get from us to the probe. So any signal we send to Voyager 1 or it sends back now takes a full day as the spacecraft continues to explore interstellar space. To celebrate the major milestone for the farthest human-made object in history, the Empire State Building in New York City lit up in gold . This golden glow references the Golden Record onboard both the Voyager 1 and 2 spacecraft. And the Empire State Building wasn't the only major landmark to celebrate the occasion. The Space Needle in Seattle, Washington, and both the Willis Tower and the Skydeck Chicago in Chicago, Illinois have all been illuminated gold to mark the milestone. Why is it incredible? The Golden Record that these gold glowing buildings are referencing serves as an inanimate ambassador for Earth , carrying information about humanity, our planet, the other species who live here, the languages we speak, the music we listen to and so much more. It even includes instructions for building a record player to play the record. The Voyager mission has, and continues to, make incredible scientific discoveries and observations throughout our solar system and now in interstellar space. But this Golden Record provides an additional aspect to the mission that connects us here on Earth to whatever unknown life may exist out there. If some sort of life forms out in the cosmos were to ever come across Voyager and its Golden Record at any point in the distant future, they might learn a little bit about our small blue dot.

top.description: By Ike Uchechukwu, Calabar Gunmen have killed a 60-year-old man, James Edi Diwa, and set his body and motorcycle ablaze in Boki Local Government Area of Cross River State. The incident reportedly occurred at about 5:20pm along the Isobendeghe–Boje Road, where Diwa, a native of Katchuan in Irruan community, was riding his motorcycle when he was ambushed. The attackers allegedly shot him, beheaded him and set his remains and motorcycle on fire. The Cross River State Police Command disclosed this in a statement on Thursday by its Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Eitokpah Sunday. According to the police, the deceased’s wife, Mrs Schola Abang, reported the incident at the Boki Divisional Police Headquarters on November 13, 2026, at about 6:10am. The statement said police operatives visited the scene following the report and commenced preliminary investigations. “The Cross River State Police Command has commenced an investigation into the gruesome murder of a 60-year-old man, identified as James Edi Diwa, who was allegedly ambushed and killed by unidentified gunmen along the Isobendeghe–Boje Road in Boki Local Government Area,” the statement said. The Commissioner of Police, Mr Ajo Geoffrey Ordue, condemned the killing and directed relevant operational and investigative units to intensify efforts to identify and arrest those responsible. The command said no arrest had been made as of the time the statement was issued. Ordue assured residents that the police would work to bring the perpetrators to justice. He urged members of the public to remain calm, refrain from taking the law into their hands and provide credible information that could assist the investigation. top.title: 2027: ACF warns of emerging political violence, urges restraint
top.description: …Forum urges Tinubu, governors to ensure fairness to opposition By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo The Arewa Consultative Forum (ACF) has raised concerns over emerging signs of political violence ahead of the 2027 general elections, urging political leaders, security agencies and Nigerians to embrace restraint and protect democratic values. The forum warned that provocative demonstrations, stone-throwing, abusive chants and attacks on individuals could undermine the country’s democratic process and heighten political tensions. In a statement issued by its National Publicity Secretary, Prof. Tukur Muhammad-Baba, the ACF described the development, particularly in major urban centres, as unacceptable, dangerous and condemnable. It expressed concern over reports and videos circulating in conventional and social media showing acts of provocation directed at politically exposed personalities and other high-profile individuals. The forum also condemned the use of physical violence, looting and arson to express political grievances, warning that abusive reactions to such incidents could further escalate tensions. According to the ACF, although political violence is not new in Nigeria’s electoral history, the country should have moved beyond practices that undermine its democratic development and contradict its societal values. It warned that political intolerance, incivility and disregard for law and order posed serious threats to democratic progress and the country’s future. The forum urged Nigerians to embrace calmness and civility, stressing that the legitimate way to express political dissatisfaction was through the use of their Permanent Voter Cards to vote in accordance with the law. It called on community stakeholders, socio-cultural organisations, trade groups, non-governmental organisations, traditional rulers, religious leaders and other citizens to intensify public enlightenment on the dangers of political intolerance and electoral violence. The ACF also urged political office holders, particularly President Bola Tinubu and state governors, to demonstrate fairness, equity and tolerance towards perceived or actual political opponents. It further called on authorities to ensure that opposition parties had unhindered access to public facilities for their campaign activities. The forum urged security agencies to respond firmly but professionally to emerging threats through coordinated and intelligence-driven measures. While commending the recent presidential pardon granted to citizens arrested in connection with the violence, the ACF said attention should now shift towards preventive measures to avert further incidents. It stressed that protecting democratic values and ensuring peaceful political activities ahead of the 2027 elections required collective responsibility from political leaders, security agencies and citizens. top.title: I never planned to have two wives, 18 children – Veteran actor Oga Bello
top.description: Veteran Nollywood actor Adebayo Salami, popularly known as Oga Bello, has revealed that he never envisaged having two wives and 18 children, saying he initially wanted a simple family life with just one wife. The 73-year-old actor made the revelation during an appearance on the Talk to B podcast, where he spoke about his marriage, family and how life took a different turn from what he had originally planned. Salami said his initial dream was to have a small family, inspired by the marriage of his godfather, Femi Okunnu, whose lifestyle he admired. “I never planned to have a large family. All I wanted was a simple life with my wife, but life took a different direction. “Today, I see my children as part of my destiny,” he said. He recalled how he and his wife enjoyed spending time together, particularly having breakfast before he left for work, describing the arrangement as the kind of family life he had always wanted. However, he said his growing fame changed the course of his personal life and made it difficult to maintain the arrangement he had initially envisioned. The actor also recounted an incident in which two women gave birth to his children within the same week, describing the experience as overwhelming. According to him, he was making preparations for the naming ceremony of one child when he received news that another woman had also delivered a baby for him. Despite the unexpected expansion of his family, Salami said he had no regrets, noting that he now considers his large family part of his destiny. The veteran actor has two wives and 18 children, comprising nine sons and nine daughters. One of his children is popular Nollywood actor and filmmaker Femi Adebayo, and another named Tope Adebayo, who is also an actor. He also disclosed that he never imagined some of his children would eventually follow his footsteps into the entertainment industry. top.title: Coinbase Launches U.S. Spot Margin Trading With Up to 10x Leverage
top.description: Bitcoin Magazine Coinbase Launches U.S. Spot Margin Trading With Up to 10x Leverage Coinbase (COIN) has opened crypto spot margin trading to U.S. customers, letting eligible traders borrow to go long or short with up to 10x leverage, the exchange announced Wednesday, though access is limited to investors with more than $10 million invested. “Crypto spot margin is now available in the US for eligible traders,” Coinbase wrote on X. Traders borrow at the moment they place an order, rather than setting up a loan first. The eligibility bar is high. In a follow-up post , Coinbase said margin trading is open only to people who qualify as “eligible contract participants” under the Commodity Exchange Act. For an individual, that generally means more than $10 million in assets invested on a discretionary basis. The product is also not available in all states, and the loans are for commercial or business purposes only, the company said. Coinbase did not list eligible states or assets in the posts. The limit tracks how U.S. law treats leverage. Under the Commodity Exchange Act , leveraged retail commodity trades generally have to run through a regulated futures exchange, so off-exchange margin products like this one are often reserved for eligible contract participants. How spot margin works Coinbase first described spot margin in October. Eligible traders can borrow against collateral to increase their buying power on spot markets, with leverage of up to 10x on selected major assets and up to 5x on other supported assets. Collateral can be posted in more than 15 supported assets and stays on Coinbase throughout. Loan balances, collateral levels and margin health appear in real time, and spot positions sit in the same margin portfolio as a trader’s derivatives. For U.S. customers, Coinbase Credit, Inc. makes the loans and Coinbase, Inc. holds the collateral as custodian. The company said spot margin is not a product of Coinbase Financial Markets, its regulated U.S. futures broker. The risk disclosures are blunt. Variable-rate interest accrues hourly and can erode a trader’s margin level, and market moves can trigger margin calls or automatic liquidation. In October, the company warned that collateral “may be liquidated without notice” and that traders can lose more than their initial deposit. Part of a bigger trading push from Coinbase Spot margin is one piece of what Coinbase calls its “Everything Exchange.” In the same October post, it said its integration of Deribit was complete and that crypto options, spot margin and unified portfolios would roll out in the coming weeks. The Synergy deal, which Capita values at £370 million, covers HR, payroll, finance, and other back-office services across four government departments and nearly 100 arm's-length bodies. PCS wants the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP), which leads the program, to bring the work in-house. "The ongoing Capita pensions scandal has left civil servants facing financial hardship, distress and uncertainty. "How many more warnings does the government need? In Parliament, MPs have challenged Capita's record, highlighted the devastating consequences of pension administration failures and questioned the wisdom of handing the company even greater responsibility. "PCS has warned for years about the dangers of outsourcing essential public services. We need accountability. We need answers. And we need a government that puts public servants before private profit. Stop the Capita Synergy contract. Bring these vital services back in-house." nigeria.title: VeryDarkMan hospitalised in China after severe malaria scare
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Social media activist Martins Otse, popularly known as VeryDarkMan, says he nearly died after developing what doctors in China described as a life-threatening form of malaria. In a video shared on Thursday, the 32-year-old said he was admitted to hospital and placed in quarantine after his condition worsened. He said he had initially ignored a doctor’s warning and taken oral medication obtained through members of the Nigerian community in China. VeryDarkMan said he first visited a hospital where tests showed he had malaria. According to him, a doctor warned that it was a severe case requiring urgent treatment through his veins. He said he later contacted a doctor friend in Nigeria, who reportedly told him it was a common form of malaria. Doubting the Chinese doctor’s advice, VeryDarkMan said he left the hospital and sought medication. “Before I left, the doctor looked at me and told me, ‘They have to make things go through your veins. Oral is not going to work. It’s going to make it worse,’” he said. VeryDarkMan said the first medication he received had expired, so he asked for another dose. He initially felt better after taking it, but said his condition deteriorated that night. “My brothers and sisters, yesterday night, I swear to God, I nearly died, bro. No jokes. Exactly what the doctor said. The drugs turned against me. It became two times worse,” he said. He said he returned to hospital and was told to remain there. nigeria.title: Joshua unable to see newborn daughter until after Tyson Fury fight
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Anthony Joshua says he will not meet his newborn daughter in person until after his December 11 fight against Tyson Fury, as he remains in training camp in Marbella. In an interview with The Sun, the British heavyweight described his daughter’s arrival as “amazing” and “a big blessing”, but said he wished he could have been present for her birth. He has spoken with the baby and her mother, Nicole, through FaceTime. “It’s not ideal but she is in good hands,” Joshua said. “She’s got an amazing mother, she’s got amazing family round her and the people at the hospital, I heard they were amazing. I spoke to them and said thank you, so I’m pretty content at the minute that she’s in good hands. But, for me, it would have been much better if I was able to be there.” The 37-year-old said he had committed to the fight preparations months ago and could not change his plans. “But I’m on duty at the minute and we’re on a mission. I knew about this nine months ago so I made this commitment that I can’t change, unfortunately, but there will be many more birthdays I’ll be at, for sure,” he said. Asked when he expected to meet his daughter, Joshua said: “Probably December 12, December 13. “I’ll go and check in and rock her to sleep, let her hear my voice and let her feel my heartbeat, really. I’m going to definitely do it all,” he said. “You might see me with some eye shadow on, some nail polish on, drinking some tea in a doll’s playhouse just trying to do the right thing by her.” Joshua said he wanted to give JJ a sibling after the “painful and traumatic” experience of last December’s car crash in Nigeria, which killed two members of his team, personal trainer Latif Ayodele and strength and conditioning coach Sina Ghami. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Coinbase Launches U.S. Spot Margin Trading With Up to 10x Leverage Coinbase (COIN) has opened crypto spot margin trading to U.S. customers, letting eligible traders borrow to go long or short with up to 10x leverage, the exchange announced Wednesday, though access is limited to investors with more than $10 million invested. “Crypto spot margin is now available in the US for eligible traders,” Coinbase wrote on X. Traders borrow at the moment they place an order, rather than setting up a loan first. The eligibility bar is high. In a follow-up post , Coinbase said margin trading is open only to people who qualify as “eligible contract participants” under the Commodity Exchange Act. For an individual, that generally means more than $10 million in assets invested on a discretionary basis. The product is also not available in all states, and the loans are for commercial or business purposes only, the company said. Coinbase did not list eligible states or assets in the posts. The limit tracks how U.S. law treats leverage. Under the Commodity Exchange Act , leveraged retail commodity trades generally have to run through a regulated futures exchange, so off-exchange margin products like this one are often reserved for eligible contract participants. How spot margin works Coinbase first described spot margin in October. Eligible traders can borrow against collateral to increase their buying power on spot markets, with leverage of up to 10x on selected major assets and up to 5x on other supported assets. Collateral can be posted in more than 15 supported assets and stays on Coinbase throughout. Loan balances, collateral levels and margin health appear in real time, and spot positions sit in the same margin portfolio as a trader’s derivatives. For U.S. customers, Coinbase Credit, Inc. makes the loans and Coinbase, Inc. holds the collateral as custodian. The company said spot margin is not a product of Coinbase Financial Markets, its regulated U.S. futures broker. The risk disclosures are blunt. Variable-rate interest accrues hourly and can erode a trader’s margin level, and market moves can trigger margin calls or automatic liquidation. In October, the company warned that collateral “may be liquidated without notice” and that traders can lose more than their initial deposit. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Russia’s Central Bank to Let Retail Investors Trade Bitcoin on Margin Russia’s central bank plans to let ordinary investors trade bitcoin and other crypto on margin, capped at 300,000 rubles with a broker, a senior Bank of Russia official said this week, days after retail buying became legal. Olga Shishlyannikova, director of the central bank’s department of investment financial intermediaries, outlined the plan at the Ural Conference hosted by NAUFOR, the national association of securities market participants, RBC Investments reported. She said the margin rule and two other acts are under review at Russia’s Justice Ministry, and the regulator expects them to be registered by the end of 2026. It is not yet clear whether the 300,000-ruble margin limit for non-qualified investors will be shared with the existing cap on crypto purchases or counted separately. The central bank first published draft margin rules in July. Under that draft, brokers could accept cryptocurrencies as collateral for margin positions, and their clients could sell short. Both qualified and non-qualified investors would be able to trade on margin, with retail crypto trades subject to limits set by the Bank of Russia. The draft also added crypto to the risk-coverage ratios brokers use to police leveraged trades. Those ratios set how far a broker can lend against a client’s portfolio and when positions are forcibly closed. Crypto funds expected in 2027 Shishlyannikova also said the central bank expects the first Russian mutual funds that hold crypto directly to appear in 2027. Professional market participants have already filed applications to register such funds, she said. “Yes, we are considering the possibility next year of amending the relevant regulations to allow funds intended for qualified investors to buy cryptocurrency,” Shishlyannikova said. The regulator is not considering the same access for funds sold to non-qualified investors, she added. In late September, the central bank allowed fund managers to invest qualified investors’ money in cash-settled instruments tied to crypto prices, in a directive registered with the Justice Ministry. entertainment.description: “Men are not wired to show emotions.” A male friend once said to me during an argument. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. entertainment.description: Growing up, Tunji Olowolafe ’s parents brought the family to Are-Ekiti every Christmas, and a trip to Ikogosi was compulsory. Dr. Olowolafe said Ikogosi’s task now is to give visitors compelling reasons to come, stay longer and spend across local businesses. He pointed to the recent Ikogosi 17.5km Race, which drew runners from across Nigeria alongside athletes from Ghana, Kenya and Ethiopia, as an example of what happens when private initiative meets local hospitality. He urged the same thinking for lifestyle and executive tourism, with the ambition of making Ikogosi a premier international destination for weddings, milestone birthdays, corporate retreats and landmark gatherings. “Our natural landscape will draw people in. entertainment.title: Beyoncé Becomes First Artist in Grammy History to Earn 100 Nominations!
entertainment.description: Beyoncé becomes the first artist in history to reach 100 career Grammy nominations. Photo Credit: Beyoncé/Instagram If you have ever wondered what triple digits look like on music’s biggest stage, Beyoncé just gave everyone the answer. The Houston-born global music superstar has officially become the first artist in history to reach 100 career Grammy nominations, hitting the milestone with her latest nod for “ Morning Dew ( Donk )”, which is nominated for Best R&B Solo Performance at the 69th Annual Grammy Awards (2027 Grammys). Released in July 2026 ahead of the 20th anniversary of her sophomore album B’Day, “Morning Dew (Donk)” puts her in a category alongside Kehlani , Victoria Monét , Jill Scott , and Nigerian star Tems . To put the 100-nomination milestone into perspective, no other recording artist has ever crossed into triple digits since the Grammys began. Beyoncé had previously been tied with her husband, Jay-Z , at 88 nominations each before breaking that tie in 2024 with 11 nods for Cowboy Carter to reach 99—and this latest recognition pushes her even further ahead as the artist with the highest number of Grammy nominations in history. Beyoncé holding her three Grammy trophies at the 67th Annual Grammy Awards in 2025. Photo Credit: Beyoncé/Instagram It is also a good reminder of how long she has been doing this at the highest level. Beyoncé’s Grammy journey started all the way back in 2000 as part of Destiny’s Child with “Bills, Bills, Bills”, and across more than two decades as a solo artist, group member, and collaborator, she has built a record that keeps stretching further ahead of the pack. Alongside holding the title for the most Grammy nominations of all time, she is already the most awarded artist in Grammy history with 35 wins, a record she first broke in 2023 when she surpassed late conductor Georg Solti ’s 31 trophies. She pushed that tally even higher at the 2025 Grammys, taking home three awards—Album of the Year and Best Country Album for Cowboy Carter, as well as Best Country Duo/Group Performance for “II Most Wanted” alongside Miley Cyrus . Now all eyes turn to Sunday, 7 February 2027, when the 2027 Grammy Awards take place at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles and we find out whether nomination number 100 turns into Grammy win number 36. technology.title: Mouse fight club might explain why we like to watch violent things
technology.description: Credit: J.M. Iravedra-Garcia et al., 2026 Credit: J.M. Iravedra-Garcia et al., 2026 There's something about watching violent events that broadly appeals to us, whether it's the latest John Wick movie, a video game, or a live UFC bout. Scientists have debated whether watching violent things could make us more aggressive, but it could also be an adaptive survival strategy. Male mice, for instance, who watch other mice fighting learned enough about how to fight to better protect themselves (compared to mice who didn't watch fights) when pitted against stronger, more aggressive opponents, according to a paper published in the journal Nature. The team assigned male mice randomly to three different groups—fighters, spectators, or novices—and then subjected each group to eight days of training involving three 10-minute sessions per day. The novices played with stuffed mice in isolation, while the spectators watched various pairs of fighter mice battle it out from a raised platform behind a transparent barrier—a set-up chosen to let them smell and listen to the fights as well as observe them. The ninth day was "fight night," when all the mice had to face a daunting opponent in three 4-minute rounds. Each fight was filmed from above so that the mouse behavior could be analyzed. To monitor corresponding changes in brain activity, the team engineered the rodents' excitatory brain cells to glow green whenever they were activated, while inhibitory brain cells glowed red. They also implanted tiny optical fibers into 12 interconnected brain regions so they could track changing activity in every brain region simultaneously. Read full article Comments

technology.title: Qualcomm offers test drive of its rack-scale Nvidia AI challenger
technology.description: Qualcomm has opened cloud-based trials of its Dragonfly AI200 rack-scale inference system to selected customers through Cirrascale Cloud Services. Dragonfly AI200 is Qualcomm's pitch for running large language, multimodal, and other AI models without Nvidia-sized power and operating bills. Whether it delivers those savings is something customers can now put to the test on Cirrascale's AI Innovation Cloud, with a route into production deployments, Qualcomm says. Cirrascale also demonstrated the system at SC26 in Chicago on November 17-18. The AI200 is part of Qualcomm's Dragonfly datacenter lineup, which also includes the AI250 and AI300 accelerators and the C1000 server CPU. The company set out its broader ambitions at its Investor Day in June . Each AI200 accelerator card carries 768 GB of LPDDR memory, with 56 cards providing about 43 TB in a liquid-cooled rack. Qualcomm says the system supports models ranging from 7 billion to 10 trillion parameters, including long-context, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and agentic workloads. As we previously explored , packing in memory doesn't necessarily mean matching Nvidia's performance. Its Blackwell-based NVL72 systems use fast – and costly – HBM3e stacks, while Qualcomm has opted for LPDDR, more commonly found in mobile devices. "AI inference is becoming one of the largest and most important computing workloads in the datacenter, and the industry needs a more efficient approach," said Tony Pialis, Qualcomm's executive vice president and general manager for datacenter. He claimed that the AI200 brings the company's experience with high-performance, low-power computing to a rack-scale infrastructure, in an architecture designed around the performance, memory, and cost requirements of inference workloads. "Our customers need efficient, scalable infrastructure that can support increasingly sophisticated models without allowing power and operating costs to become the limiting factor," said Cirrascale CEO Dave Driggers. "By working with Qualcomm, we can give customers evaluation access to a compelling new architecture purpose-built for the next generation of AI inference." The chip firm also has its own software stack, the Dragonfly AI Infrastructure Management Suite, for provisioning, monitoring, workload orchestration, and fault handling across rack-scale deployments. ®

technology.title: Voyager 1 celebrates one light-day with a nice lie-down
technology.description: Voyager 1 marked its milestone of one light-day from Earth in time-honored fashion: by giving controllers the silent treatment. On November 14, the mission team noticed that the veteran spacecraft had stopped returning science and engineering data. A Deep Space Network antenna in Canberra, Australia, picked up its carrier signal, but no data. The carrier signal indicates that Voyager 1 can still keep its antenna pointed at Earth and operate its transmitting equipment. However, something could be amiss with the system responsible for collecting and collating data from the spacecraft. Something similar happened in 2023 . After a few months of troubleshooting, engineers managed to coax a response from the probe, and by June 2024, NASA was delighted to announce that the spacecraft was back in action. The problem was traced to a faulty computer chip, and engineers devised a software update to work around the defective hardware. That experience will stand the team in good stead this time around. There was also a brief interruption in communications with Voyager 1 in October, which could have been caused by the spacecraft dropping into safe mode after a thruster failover occurred. Engineers are investigating whether the two incidents are connected. The Voyagers have an impressive amount of fault protection built in, which has contributed to their extraordinary longevity. It will be half a century in 2027 since the spacecraft were launched, so glitches are understandable and likely. NASA expects to confirm on November 19 that Voyager 1 was still operating when it reached one light-day from Earth on November 18, using its carrier signal and trajectory calculations. The day's delay neatly illustrates a major headache for engineers: communication latency. It now takes more than 24 hours for commands to reach the spacecraft, and the same amount of time for a response to be received. Diagnosing the fault could therefore take weeks or longer. ®

technology.title: Microsoft To Do will soon become Microsoft Done
technology.description: Microsoft has slipped some bad news into this week's Ignite AI puffery: the To Do apps are retiring on June 30, 2027, ending a journey that began with its acquisition of Wunderlist more than a decade ago. The confirmation came in an announcement about unified tasks and plans for Copilot and Microsoft 365. Until now, there was To Do or Planner (in basic or premium guise). The idea is "a single system for tracking your work as an individual, as a team, and as an organization." To Do contributes features to that future, but its apps don't get to join it. The problem is that Planner doesn't do everything To Do does. Microsoft would like users to migrate to Planner but, by the company's own admission , there are plenty of gaps. No native Windows or Mac desktop apps are planned to replace To Do; file attachments aren't supported on tasks in the Planner private plan, and there's no equivalent to To Do list groups in Planner. "Equivalent To Do printing and email-list capabilities are not currently planned for the replacement experience," and so on. Existing To Do tasks and lists won't migrate to Planner either. They'll remain accessible through Planner until June 30, 2027, but that access ends with the apps. Microsoft says the date does not itself trigger deletion of the underlying data. Personal Microsoft account holders are left in an even worse state: Planner isn't available to them, including Microsoft 365 Personal and Family subscribers. Microsoft's advice is to choose another task-management app and prepare to export their data. Export instructions are still to come, and exporting won't necessarily produce something another app can import. Very much a case of "don't let the door hit you on the way out." Unifying tasks and plans is a good idea – the current situation does create confusion, as Microsoft acknowledged. However, taking an axe to To Do, which was developed to be a successor to Wunderlist ( acquired in 2015 for a figure between $100 million and $200 million, an early action under Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella), seems extreme. Microsoft calls the replacement "a unified platform for people and agents across Microsoft 365" and stated: "This unified platform makes accessing Planner through Copilot, Cowork and Autopilot easier." Some users responding to the announcement were unimpressed, with one declaring "What a mess," and another asking if To Do might be spun off into an open source project: "Not everything needs to be put into an AI/Copilot agent." Indeed, it doesn't. But a useful service that doesn't ram Copilot and AI integration down customers' throats at every opportunity? That would never do. The message for To Do users appears to be: Get with the Plan(ner) or just get out. ®

science.description: null The Empire State Building is illuminated in gold to celebrate Voyager 1 hitting one light-day from Earth, seen here on Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026, from SUMMIT One Vanderbilt in New York City. (Image credit: NASA/Bill Ingalls) The Empire State Building glowed in glittering gold last night (Nov. 17) to celebrate NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft hitting one light-day from Earth. And it isn't the only building celebrating this achievement with a sparkling display. What is it? Today (Nov. 18) at 5:16 a.m. EST (1016 GMT), NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft hit one light-day from Earth. About 16 billion miles (about 26 billion kilometers) away, this is the point at which it takes a full day (or 24 hours) for one light particle to get from us to the probe. So any signal we send to Voyager 1 or it sends back now takes a full day as the spacecraft continues to explore interstellar space. To celebrate the major milestone for the farthest human-made object in history, the Empire State Building in New York City lit up in gold . This golden glow references the Golden Record onboard both the Voyager 1 and 2 spacecraft. And the Empire State Building wasn't the only major landmark to celebrate the occasion. The Space Needle in Seattle, Washington, and both the Willis Tower and the Skydeck Chicago in Chicago, Illinois have all been illuminated gold to mark the milestone. Why is it incredible? The Golden Record that these gold glowing buildings are referencing serves as an inanimate ambassador for Earth , carrying information about humanity, our planet, the other species who live here, the languages we speak, the music we listen to and so much more. It even includes instructions for building a record player to play the record. The Voyager mission has, and continues to, make incredible scientific discoveries and observations throughout our solar system and now in interstellar space. But this Golden Record provides an additional aspect to the mission that connects us here on Earth to whatever unknown life may exist out there. If some sort of life forms out in the cosmos were to ever come across Voyager and its Golden Record at any point in the distant future, they might learn a little bit about our small blue dot.

Credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech NASA’s Voyager 1 probe, humanity’s farthest-flying spacecraft, has reached one light-day from Earth, after more than 49 years of constant travel. A light-day is the distance light travels in 24 hours, equaling about 16.1 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers). The spacecraft achieved the milestone at 2:16 a.m. PST (5:16 a.m. EST) Nov. 18. Voyager team members at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California, managed by Caltech, heard from the probe 24 hours later, the time it took for the spacecraft’s radio signal traveling at the speed of light to reach Earth, early Thursday. “Traveling a light-day is a singular feat for a spacecraft, but Voyager is so much more than a distant traveler. Light travels at about 186,000 miles (299,000 kilometers) a second in a vacuum. A ray of sunlight passing Earth takes about 1.3 seconds to reach the Moon, about four hours to reach Neptune, and another 20 hours to reach Voyager 1. For comparison, a light-year is 5.88 trillion miles (9.46 trillion kilometers). The nonprofit Common Space plans to assemble a six-spacecraft constellation of Earth-observing satellites , whose high-resolution imagery will aid first responders, journalists, scientists and human-rights investigators around the world. That plan firmed up a bit today (Nov. 19), as Common Space announced the builder of the first of those satellites : Satellogic, an Argentine-U.S. geospatial intelligence company. There are more than 1,000 Earth-observing satellites circling our planet at the moment. But much of the data they gather is proprietary or too expensive to serve the common good, according to Common Space. The nonprofit wants to change that via its envisioned constellation, which it says will collect imagery specifically for humanitarian and public-interest purposes. Common Space plans to operate on a "club-good model," which will share infrastructure and costs across a large community, allowing extensive, low-cost access to high-quality imagery. Satellogic is now officially part of this picture. "With Satellogic as our spacecraft partner, we're moving from vision to orbit and putting high-resolution data into the hands of those who need it most," Common Space co-founder Rhiannan Price said in a statement today. "This isn't just another satellite. We're building infrastructure to serve people for years to come." The satellite is Satellogic's NewSat Mark V, which Common Space selected after a competitive request-for-proposal process. Satellites can help first responders deal with natural disasters. science.title: What's next for NASA interstellar Voyager 1 probe after passing 1 light-day from Earth?
science.description: null Voyager 1 has reached a historic milestone in space — it now takes a light-day to send a command to the spacecraft, meaning a full 24 hours for Earth to hail the distant spacecraft. Since Voyager 1 and its twin, Voyager 2 , launched on an initial tour through the outer solar system in 1977, their missions have been packed with science. Voyager 1 looked at Jupiter and Saturn from up close before veering for a flyby of Saturn's moon Titan and Saturn's rings, a pathway that brought it above the plane of the solar system in the early 1980s. Voyager 1's faster path out of the solar system brought it to one light-day in distance on Wednesday (Nov. 18), while Voyager 2 — which took a slightly slower track to see Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune — will reach a light-day of distance in 2035. So what's next for the two Voyager spacecraft as they reach further into interstellar space? Exploring afar Interstellar space, which is the area where the sun's constant stream of solar particles within the heliopause gives way to the physics of interstellar space, has been a valuable harvest for both Voyagers. Voyager 1 crossed interstellar space in August 2012 and continues to get data, while Voyager 2 has done the same since November 2018. "Current science is continuing our investigation on magnetic field strength and direction, plasma density, and energetic particle detection. What is important is to measure how these phenomena change as the spacecraft travels further away from the sun," Suzanne Dodd, project manager for the Voyager missions at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), told Space.com in an email. Added to that will be the Voyagers' examinations of plasma and magnetic fields nearby the spacecraft, and a focus on any "solar effects" such as shocks or pressure fronts, added JPL project scientist Linda Spilker in an email. "Key Voyager science going forward includes observing the extent to which our sun continues to affect interstellar space, all the way out to Voyager 1," Spilker continued. "Where does the sun's influence end and pristine interstellar space begin? Perhaps Voyager may last long enough to answer that question." The team also wants to watch the magnetic field around the spacecraft continue to change direction from the sun, to interstellar space, Spilker noted. That finding was not expected when the Voyagers launched, so scientists are curious to know more — as long as the spacecraft can last, that is. science.description: It sounds idyllic. Who wouldn’t want to occupy a newly built residence in the Florida Keys, complete with its own coral garden right outside the window? The only complication is that it is 17 metres below the surface of the Atlantic Ocean. That is not putting off Jim Brittsan, though. “This is really exciting,” he says. Brittsan is the founder and executive director of coral restoration non-profit Sustainable Ocean and Reefs (SOAR). He is also the diver who arranged the temporary coral nursery beside the residence, having brought the corals from a site where, 10 metres closer to the surface, they faced increasing environmental stress. Now, in reduced temperatures, they are starting to flourish, hosting their own marine life – visible day and night, in all its busyness, from the underwater residence known as Vanguard just 15 metres away. Vanguard was deployed at Tennessee Reef in June 2026 DEEP and Brendan Hall Vanguard is a long-stay underwater station for marine biologists. It was deployed in June 2026 at Tennessee Reef on the seafloor of the Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary, around 8 kilometres south of Long Key. Its coral nursery looks like a strange marine shrubbery: the coral fragments are arranged on anchored ropes that stand upright in the water. Once Vanguard is operational, a more permanent nursery will be established and the corals will eventually be planted on the seabed as part of ongoing restoration efforts, with their long-term survival assessed through monitoring. Advertisement Resident scientists will be able to monitor marine life around the clock DEEP, the international design and engineering organisation that built Vanguard, aims to make humans aquatic by establishing more subsea habitats like it. These will allow people to live underwater for extended periods to engage in scientific research and conservation. This opens up unprecedented opportunities to do research because there is no need for divers to bounce up and down to a research vessel on the surface. science.description: Turmeric capsules are touted as remedies for joint problems olga Yastremska/Alamy Turmeric supplements seem to have little to no effect on pain and mobility problems caused by knee osteoarthritis. That’s according to one of the most rigorous assessments of the evidence yet, which focused on four randomised controlled trials comparing the supplements to placebo pills. Osteoarthritis, which affects more than 500 million people worldwide , is caused by damage to cartilage that cushions the ends of bones, resulting in pain, stiffness and inflammation. Standard treatments include painkillers and anti-inflammatory drugs that can ease symptoms. “But many people see little or no benefit,” says Philip Conaghan at the University of Leeds, UK, who wasn’t involved in the latest review. Read more There are only a few anti-ageing supplements that actually work Turmeric supplements are often touted as an alternative therapy. They contain curcumin, a compound that gives turmeric its yellow colour and is thought to have anti-inflammatory properties. Yet such beliefs are often based on prior flawed studies , says Ivan Shirinsky at the Research Institute of Internal and Preventive Medicine in Novosibirsk, Russia. Advertisement Shirinsky and his colleagues analysed results from four randomised controlled trials, collectively involving more than 370 participants with knee osteoarthritis. Participants were randomly assigned to take either a supplement containing turmeric extract or placebo pills two or three times per day, for between eight weeks and three months. Each trial used a slightly different supplement containing a different curcumin dose. “We looked at the most rigorous evidence available,” says Shirinsky. Among those who took a placebo, knee pain decreased by 1.6 points, on average, on a scale from 0 to 10 by the end of the study. Those taking turmeric supplements experienced an average 2.3-point decrease in pain, meaning the difference between the turmeric and placebo groups was half that required to be meaningful to patients based on prior studies , says Shirinsky. science.description: null Astronomers may have, for the first time ever, directly witnessed a star engulfing its companion, a new study reports. As stars die, they swell up to hundreds of times their original size, consuming anything orbiting nearby. In a binary star system, this can include a dying star merging with its companion star. However, scientists had never directly seen any examples of such a cosmic drama unfolding — until now. "Catching a star engulfing its companion in the act is very difficult," study lead author Viraj Karambelkar, an astrophysicist at Columbia University in New York, told Space.com. "When a star engulfs its companion, its effect is very subtle — like throwing a bucket of water in a large ocean. We need sensitive telescopes monitoring the sky for a long time in order to catch this effect." In December 2025, observations from NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope provided the final evidence that allowed researchers to fully reconstruct what happened before, during, and after the merger of a binary star system nicknamed Bao in the Andromeda galaxy. The star is about seven times heftier and 350 times wider than our own sun . In 2023, using NASA's now-defunct NEOWISE space telescope and the WINTER telescope at Palomar Observatory in California, the scientists noticed that this star was brightening. By analyzing previous records, they found that the red giant had gradually started growing more luminous in 2018. The researchers had previously suggested this brightening potentially occurred because the giant star engulfed a companion star. As this companion spiraled toward the giant's core, it would generate friction, heat and light, explaining the increasing luminosity. Then, near the end of 2025, the astronomers saw a giant eruption of light from this giant star. NASA's James Webb Space Telescope observed the star just 47 days after that eruption, allowing the team to characterize the event in detail. The researchers now propose that this explosion happened when a companion star about 70% the sun's mass rammed into the giant's heart. "I was absolutely flabbergasted when we saw this," Karambelkar said. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 18, 2013: NASA launches MAVEN spacecraft to Mars to find out how the Red Planet lost its water
science.description: null On Nov. 18, 2013, NASA launched the MAVEN spacecraft to Mars. The name of NASA's MAVEN spacecraft stands for Mars Atmosphere and Volatile EvolutioN. The spacecraft was an orbiter designed to help scientists figure out what happened to the water on Mars and its atmosphere. Mars is dry today, but it data from several Mars missions suggest that it was a much wetter environment a long time ago. MAVEN tracked the rate of atmospheric loss from Mars . The planet has a super thin atmosphere that has been leaking into space for a few billion years. Scientists think that when Mars lost its atmosphere, water dried up on the surface as a result. Solar storms that blast radiation into the solar system appear to have blasted away some of the atmosphere. Carbon dioxide in the atmosphere once kept Mars warm enough to sustain liquid water on its surface , and losing that greenhouse gas turned Mars into a cold and dry place. An Atlas V rocket launches NASA's Mars MAVEN orbiter into space from Florida's Cape Canaveral Space Force Base on Nov. 18, 2013. (Image credit: NASA/Bill Ingalls) Why it mattered NASA's MAVEN spacecraft was the first Mars orbiter ever built to measure how the Martian atmosphere interacts with solar wind , as well as how that constant stream of particles from the sun slowly stripped the Red Planet of its precious atmosphere over time. After its launch in 2013, MAVEN spent about 10 months en route to Mars before entering orbit on Sept. 21, 2014 . The spacecraft then spent the better part of 11 years studying the Red Planet from orbit using three different suites of instruments: An imaging ultraviolet spectrograph to study the global characteristics of the Martian atmosphere; a Neutral Gas and Ion Mass Spectromenter to measure its composition; and a six-instrument setup to study how Mars' ionosphere reacts to solar wind. An artist's view of NASA's MAVEN spacecraft at Mars on a mission to study its upper atmosphere. (Image credit: NASA) "The science MAVEN has given us is key to informing what kind of radiation protection and safety measures we must take before sending humans to Mars," Louise Prockter, NASA director of planetary science, said in June 2026 after the mission concluded. "The data collected from MAVEN will continue to provide valuable insight into Mars for decades to come." MAVEN was originally designed to study Mars for 1 full Earth year after arriving at the Red Planet. That mission ended in 2016, but the spacecraft managed to survive for another 10 years adding more observations for scientists to study. NASA ultimately began using MAVEN as a communications relay for other missions at Mars as the orbiter aged. In December 2025, MAVEN went silent , with NASA losing communication with the orbiter. science.title: Earth is missing over a billion years of geological history. Scientists may have discovered why
science.description: null More than a billion years of Earth's history has seemingly vanished. Across the planet, ancient rock formations contain colossal gaps in the geological record, leaving scientists puzzled over what happened to the missing chapters of our planet's past. Now, researchers believe they may have found an explanation, and the answer lies deep inside Earth . Normally, layers of sediment build up over time, eventually forming sedimentary rocks that preserve clues about our planet's past. Older layers generally lie beneath younger ones, allowing geologists to reconstruct ancient environments and understand how Earth has changed over billions of years. But the geological record isn't always so neatly arranged. In the Grand Canyon, rock layers separated by hundreds of millions of years sit directly on top of one another, revealing a vast gap in Earth's geological record. (Image credit: Marcia Straub via Getty Images) One of the most striking examples is found in the Grand Canyon, where rocks separated by hundreds of millions of years sit directly on top of one another, as if some force or phenomenon removed the layers that geologists would expect to see in between. This enormous gap in Earth's geological timeline is part of the phenomenon known as the Great Unconformity. It's not just the Grand Canyon. Similar gaps have been identified across Europe, Australia, Africa and Asia. Depending on the location, the missing interval ranges from approximately 200 million years to more than a billion years. "Imagine a book where a huge section in the middle has been ripped out," study lead author Santosh Dhungana said in a statement . "The Great Unconformity is that gap in Earth's story, with the narrative jumping from the early chapters straight to a much later part of the story. Our research suggests these pages weren't lost by chance." The Great Unconformity imaged here shows 550 million year old Tapeats Sandstone resting on 1.7 billion year old Vishnu Schist, in Blacktail Canyon along the Colorado River in Grand Canyon National Park, Arizona. (Image credit: William Dummitt via Getty Images) What erased the geological record? In a new study published in the journal Nature, Dhungana and study co-author Nicolas Flament investigated whether activity far below Earth's surface was to blame. Using computer models, they explored how the slow circulation of hot rock within Earth's mantle may have affected the continents over hundreds of millions of years. The results suggest that three major ancient continental regions (Laurentia (modern North America), Baltica (northern Europe) and North China were gradually pushed up during the Neoproterozoic Era, approximately one billion to 540 million years ago.
